text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it has affirmed its BBB long term rating of Australian construction group Leighton Holdings Ltd, and has revised the rating outlook to positive from stable.

"Leighton's rating reflects its position as Australia's largest construction and contract mining group benefitting from the spread of operating risk across many projects in Australia and Asia, offset by exposure to cyclical and intensely competitive sectors exhibiting low margins," S&P said.
S&P said the rating outlook is positive.

"Should Leighton sustain its operational diversity and substantial contract backlog over the next two years, and continue prudently funding concomitant capital demands, the company will likely generate performance and prudential measures consistent with a modestly higher rating," it said.
Leighton is 46 percent owned by Hochtief Ag.
S&P said leverage (total debt-to-capitalisation) was 28.6 percent at June 1996. "Leverage is likely to be in the 40-50 percent range over the medium term," S&P said.
It said the leverage ratio reflected Leighton's substantial depreciation charges and strong growth, earnings before interest and tax, depreciation and amortisation.
